name: Belotero Balance
lead: Belotero Balance is a hyaluronic acid (HA) dermal filler from Merz that uses cohesive polydensified matrix (CPM) technology, designed to integrate smoothly into the skin. It is used for fine lines and superficial areas such as nasolabial folds, and has been studied for the under-eye (infraorbital) hollow. [1][2]
Published studies include a split-face randomized comparison of three HA formulations for nasolabial folds with 12-month follow-up and trials in darker skin types and infraorbital hollows. [3][4][5]
infobox: Fine lines, nasolabial folds, infraorbital hollows

paras: A literature review describes the CPM gel family and its use for soft-tissue augmentation and rejuvenation. [1] Laboratory studies rank fillers by cohesivity and rheology and place Belotero Balance among FDA-approved HA fillers evaluated. [8][9][10]
In-vitro studies have examined how Belotero and other commercial HA fillers are degraded by hyaluronidase. [6][7]

Analyses of FDA adverse-event reports and litigation, and a cross-sectional study of complications and lawsuits involving injectable facial fillers, describe vascular and other complications for fillers as a category. [11][12]

A prospective split-face randomized study compared three HA formulations for nasolabial folds over 12 months. [3] A literature review summarizes CPM filler studies. [1] A technique article describes lip enhancement approaches. [13]

Registered trials include a post-approval nasolabial fold study (n=117), a study in Fitzpatrick skin types IV-VI (n=93), an infraorbital hollow pilot (n=66), a lidocaine pain study (n=52) and comparisons in perioral lines with Restylane Silk. [4][5][14][15]

lore.intro: On looksmax.org, Belotero appears in a thread where a user asks whether it is worthwhile as a filler before considering major facial surgery.

claims.claim: Filler can stand in for or precede major surgery
claims.believers: A looksmax.org user asked about trying Belotero before a Le Fort 3 osteotomy to see if it could provide a substantial difference. [16]
claims.experts: The published studies in this area concern soft-tissue lines, folds and hollows; no study compares filler with osteotomy. [3][5]

card.summary: Merz's soft, cohesive HA filler for fine lines and under-eye hollows, with a 12-month randomized comparison and modest forum chatter.
card.note: Studied for lines and hollows, not structural projection.

quick.overview:
Belotero Balance is a smooth hyaluronic acid filler used for fine lines, folds and the under-eye area.

A randomized split-face study followed treatment for 12 months, and trials cover several skin types.
quick.mechanism: A cohesive polydensified HA gel spreads evenly in the skin, adding subtle volume; it degrades over time and can be dissolved with hyaluronidase.
quick.risks: Filler complications reported across the category include bruising, nodules and rare vascular events. It is a prescription device given by licensed clinicians.
